statements.label: supported
statements.text: Single-cell DNA sequencing of 49,238 breast epithelial cells detected recurrent copy number alterations in a rare subpopulation of cells in almost all of the 28 samples.
statements.evidence: Using single-cell DNA sequencing (49,238 cells) of epithelium from BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers or wild-type individuals, we identified recurrent CNAs (for example, 1q-gain and 7q, 10q, 16q and 22q-loss) that are present in a rare population of cells across almost all samples (n = 28).
statements.note: The abstract reports single-cell sequencing of 49,238 cells that found recurrent CNAs in a rare population of cells across almost all 28 samples.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The proportion of breast epithelial cells carrying recurrent copy number alterations rose with the donor's age.
statements.evidence: that are present in a rare population of cells across almost all samples (n = 28)
statements.note: The abstract reports that these alterations occur in almost all samples but gives no analysis relating their frequency to donor age.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The recurrent copy number alterations were enriched in luminal cells and were not found in basal myoepithelial cells.
statements.evidence: These CNAs, common in malignant tumors, are enriched in luminal cells but absent in basal myoepithelial cells.
statements.note: The abstract states that these CNAs are enriched in luminal cells and absent in basal myoepithelial cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In carriers of BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations, the recurrent copy number alterations arise prior to LOH of the wild-type allele.
statements.evidence: In BRCA1/BRCA2 carriers, these occur before loss of heterozygosity (LOH) of wild-type alleles.
statements.note: The abstract states that in BRCA1/BRCA2 carriers these CNAs occur before LOH of the wild-type alleles.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A TGF-β-rich, immunosuppressive tumor micro-environment suppressed the adipogenic properties of the dedifferentiated tumor cells.
statements.evidence: DD tumor cells keep important biological properties of ASC including pluripotency and that their adipogenic properties are inhibited by a TGF-β-high immunosuppressive tumor micro-environment
statements.note: The abstract states that the adipogenic properties of DD tumor cells are inhibited by a TGF-β-high immunosuppressive tumor micro-environment.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tumor adipocyte stem cells carry the ancestral genomic alterations of both the well-differentiated and the dedifferentiated tumor components.
statements.evidence: We show that tumor ASC harbor the ancestral genomic alterations of WD and DD components, suggesting that both derive from these progenitors following clonal evolution.
statements.note: The abstract states that tumor ASC harbor the ancestral genomic alterations of the WD and DD components.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Within DDLPS tumors, the study identified a population of tumor adipocyte stem cells closely resembling the adipocyte stromal progenitors of white adipose tissue.
statements.evidence: We identify a population of tumor adipocyte stem cells (ASC) showing striking similarities with adipocyte stromal progenitors found in white adipose tissue.
statements.note: The abstract reports a tumor ASC population with striking similarities to the adipocyte stromal progenitors of white adipose tissue.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose DDLPS tumors contain a larger share of tumor adipocyte stem cells have worse overall survival.
statements.evidence: Using single-cell RNA sequencing, DNA sequencing, in situ multiplex immunofluorescence and functional assays in paired WD and DD components from primary DDLPS tumors, we characterize the cellular heterogeneity of DDLPS tumor and micro-environment.
statements.note: The abstract describes molecular and functional analyses of paired tumor components but reports no patient survival data.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study found 5-methylcytosine deamination signatures whose patterns were specific to tumor type, in both CpG and non-CpG sequence contexts.
statements.evidence: We uncover tumor type-specific patterns of 5mC deamination signatures in CpG and non-CpG contexts.
statements.note: The abstract reports tumor type-specific patterns of 5mC deamination signatures in CpG and non-CpG contexts.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: MBD4 was identified as the principal factor responsible for repairing 5-methylcytosine deamination in humans.
statements.evidence: Here, we establish MBD4 as the main actor responsible for 5mC deamination repair in humans.
statements.note: The abstract concludes that MBD4 is the main actor responsible for 5mC deamination repair in humans.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Tumors with inactivating MBD4 mutations respond better to immune checkpoint inhibitors than MBD4-proficient tumors.
statements.evidence: We validate our findings by modeling BER deficiencies in isogenic cell models.
statements.note: The abstract models BER deficiency in isogenic cell lines but reports nothing about how MBD4-deficient tumors respond to any therapy.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Active chromatin and early-replicating DNA, which MBD4 preferentially binds, show a lower mutational burden.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that the BER glycosylase MBD4 preferentially binds to active chromatin and early replicating DNA, which correlates with lower mutational burden in these domains.
statements.note: The abstract states that MBD4 binding to active chromatin and early replicating DNA correlates with lower mutational burden in these domains.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: A CNA-quiet subgroup occurs at a similar frequency among HPV-negative squamous cell carcinomas of the larynx and pharynx.
statements.evidence: Here, we present the hallmarks of the distinct subgroup of HPV-negative HNSCC with no or few CNAs (CNA-quiet) by genetic profiling of 802 oral cavity squamous cell carcinomas (OCSCCs).
statements.note: Only oral cavity carcinomas were profiled, so the abstract gives no frequency of CNA-quiet tumors in laryngeal or pharyngeal cancers.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with CNA-other OCSCC, patients with CNA-quiet OCSCC were older and had better 5-year overall survival.
statements.evidence: Patients with CNA-quiet OCSCC are older, more often women, less frequently current smokers, and have a better 5-year overall survival compared to CNA-other OCSCC.
statements.note: The abstract states that patients with CNA-quiet OCSCC are older and have a better 5-year overall survival than those with CNA-other OCSCC.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of the 802 oral cavity squamous cell carcinomas profiled, 73 (9.1%) had no or few copy number alterations and were classed as CNA-quiet.
statements.evidence: In total, 73 OCSCC (9.1%) are classified as CNA-quiet and 729 as CNA-other.
statements.note: The abstract reports that 73 of the 802 OCSCCs (9.1%) were classified as CNA-quiet.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tumors in the CNA-quiet group typically retained wild-type TP53 and often carried CASP8 and HRAS mutations.
statements.evidence: The CNA-quiet group is characterized by wild-type TP53, frequent CASP8 and HRAS mutations, and a less immunosuppressed tumor immune microenvironment with lower density of regulatory T cells.
statements.note: The abstract characterizes the CNA-quiet group by wild-type TP53 and frequent CASP8 and HRAS mutations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Whole-genome sequencing of 51 HPV-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinomas found that 44% of HPV integration breakpoints were subclonal.
statements.evidence: Whole-genome sequencing of 51 tumors revealed intratumor heterogeneity of HPV integration, with 44% of breakpoints subclonal
statements.note: The abstract reports that in 51 sequenced tumors 44% of HPV integration breakpoints were subclonal.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In 67% of tumors one copy of ATM was missing, and single-cell RNA sequencing and immunohistochemistry confirmed that ATM was downregulated.
statements.evidence: Heterozygous loss of ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) was observed in 67% of tumors, with its downregulation confirmed by single-cell RNA sequencing and immunohistochemistry
statements.note: The abstract reports heterozygous ATM loss in 67% of tumors, with ATM downregulation confirmed by single-cell RNA sequencing and immunohistochemistry.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose tumors had clonal HPV integration had worse overall survival than patients whose tumors lacked integration.
statements.evidence: PI3K activation was the major oncogenic mutation, with JAK-STAT activation in tumors with clonal integration and NF-kappa B activation in those without.
statements.note: The abstract compares signalling pathways between tumors with and without clonal integration but reports no survival data.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mutational signatures caused by smoking were almost absent from HPV-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinomas.
statements.evidence: HPV + HNSCCs exhibited almost no smoking-induced mutational signatures.
statements.note: The abstract states that HPV + HNSCCs exhibited almost no smoking-induced mutational signatures.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Chromosome 4p deletion is associated with shorter overall survival in patients with basal breast cancer.
statements.evidence: Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas data shows recurrent deletion of chr4p in basal breast cancer.
statements.note: The TCGA analysis shows that chr4p deletion is recurrent in basal breast cancer, but the abstract reports no survival analysis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Phylogenetic reconstruction across 23 basal breast cancers, from primary tumors and patient-derived xenografts, showed that chr4p deletion arises early in tumor evolution.
statements.evidence: Phylogenetic analysis of a panel of 23 primary tumor/patient-derived xenograft basal breast cancers reveals early evolution of chr4p deletion.
statements.note: The abstract reports that phylogenetic analysis of 23 primary tumor/PDX basal breast cancers reveals early evolution of chr4p deletion.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study linked deletion of chr4p to enhanced cell proliferation.
statements.evidence: Mechanistically we show that chr4p loss is associated with enhanced proliferation.
statements.note: The abstract states that chr4p loss is associated with enhanced proliferation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Overexpressing C4orf19, a previously unknown chr4p gene that belongs to the PDCD10-GCKIII kinase module and was named PGCKA1, suppressed proliferation.
statements.evidence: Gene function studies identify an unknown gene, C4orf19, within chr4p, which suppresses proliferation when overexpressed-a member of the PDCD10-GCKIII kinase module we name PGCKA1.
statements.note: The abstract reports that C4orf19, a chr4p gene named PGCKA1 and part of the PDCD10-GCKIII kinase module, suppresses proliferation when overexpressed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with their wild-type counterparts, chromothriptic chromosome copies showed widespread differences in topologically associated domains, chromatin accessibility, histone marks and gene expression.
statements.evidence: There were widespread differences between the chromothriptic and wild-type copies of chromosomes in topologically associated domains, chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and gene expression.
statements.note: The abstract reports widespread differences between chromothriptic and wild-type chromosome copies in TADs, chromatin accessibility, histone modifications and gene expression.

statements.note: All five organoids studied carried chromothripsis, and the abstract reports no growth comparison with organoids lacking it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Assembling each chromosome on its own and scaffolding with haplotype-resolved Hi-C reads yielded accurate assemblies despite as many as 900 structural rearrangements.

statements.note: The abstract states that separate chromosome assembly with haplotype-resolved Hi-C scaffolding produced accurate assemblies even with up to 900 structural rearrangements.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Regions within 10 kb of chromothriptic structural variants were enriched in differential epigenome peaks.
statements.evidence: Differential epigenome peaks were most enriched within 10 kb of chromothriptic structural variants.
statements.note: The abstract states that differential epigenome peaks were most enriched within 10 kb of chromothriptic structural variants.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with human MIBC, the 87 canine and 23 feline urothelial carcinomas showed a lower mutation rate and no APOBEC mutational signatures.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Dog, cat and human bladder cancers converged on shared driver genes, including ARID1A, KDM6A, TP53, FAT1 and NRAS.

statements.evidence: Bovine UC (n = 8) is distinctly different; we identify novel mutational signatures which are recapitulated in vitro in human urinary bladder UC cells treated with bracken fern extracts or purified ptaquiloside.
